detail.longDescription: FBI warns # ArtexAI # hacking tool is powering global # cyberattacks By Lawrence Abrams November 15, 2026 Excerpts: " # ARTEX is an autonomous penetration testing framework written in Go that uses artificial intelligence agents to perform reconnaissance, discover vulnerabilities, exploit systems, escalate privileges, and steal data with little human intervention. "Rather than using its own AI model, the framework integrates with external large language models ( # LLMs ), including # AnthropicClaude , # OpenAI # GPT , # DeepSeek , # GLM , # Grok , and # Kimi . "Attackers provide their goals and tasks to ARTEX, which converts them into commands executed by specialized # AIAgents . This allows them to automate intrusion activities and target multiple organizations simultaneously. "The FBI says the framework is particularly effective at identifying vulnerabilities in overlooked systems, including partner portals, employee applications, # LegacyServices , and # ThirdPartyIntegrations . "While these automated attacks can generate large volumes of suspicious traffic that trigger security alerts, their speed can leave defenders with little time to respond before attackers breach a system. "ARTEX was originally released on GitHub in July 2026 by a developer known as Autumn-27, who removed the repository on October 8 after reports emerged that threat actors were abusing the framework. "However, the FBI says the framework remains available through community forks, archived copies, localized versions, and a commercial edition called ARTEX PRO." [...] "The FBI also referenced attacks against South Korean financial institutions that exposed personal information belonging to approximately 67,000 people. "In that campaign, a Chinese-speaking threat actor combined ARTEX with # Claude Code agents to attack multiple banks, including # ShinhanBank , # KBKookminBank , and # HanaBank ."
